data.title: July Fourth, 1862—At Sea
data.description: What was Independence Day like aboard a sailing ship in the middle of the ocean? Join us for the story of six-year-old Sara Delano, future mother of Franklin D. Roosevelt, who spent 128 days at sea traveling to China in 1862. Drawn from a firsthand Roosevelt family journal, this talk reveals a world of tall ships, global voyages, and a Fourth of July celebration complete with cake, ice cream, and cannon fire.
data.location: Franklin Delano Roosevelt Memorial (meet the ranger in the exhibit area of the park store)

data.title: The Unfinished America: A 250-Year Journey of Liberty and Economic Freedom
data.description:
Meet at the World War II Kiosk and join a National Park Service volunteer for an immersive 90-minute walking tour exploring the evolution of individual liberty and economic freedom while visiting several National Mall monuments and memorials. From the towering legacy of George Washington to the revolutionary courage of the 56 Signers of the Declaration of Independence, we will trace America’s fitful yet persistent progress toward a "more perfect union." This journey weaves together iconic sites with personal stories of stowaways, soldiers, and the "Greatest Generation" to honor the sacrifices that built our modern world.

As we celebrate this year's historic semiquincentennial, you are invited to connect your own family’s legacy to our shared pursuit of freedom and learn about nationwide celebrations ahead. Discover why the torch lit 250 years ago remains an exceptional beacon of democratic leadership in the world today. Memorials visited include: WWII and Washington Monument, Japanese Lantern, Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial, Korean and Vietnam War Memorials, the Lincoln Memorial, and Signers' Island.

Walk is less then 2 miles.
data.location: World War II Memorial (contact station)

data.title: Tales of the Odd and Unusual
data.description: Join a park ranger for a program that celebrates the spirit of Halloween but without the supernatural. There have been two hundred and fifty years of strange happenings on the National Mall and around Washington. Together, we’ll explore true Washington tales of the strange, the unusual, and the just plain odd.
